methods.name: Knowledge Graph Curation Framework
methods.description: A practical framework proposed for improving the quality of KGs, involving assessment, cleaning, and enrichment.

methods.name: Knowledge Assessment
methods.description: The first step in KG curation, involving assessing the status of KGs based on quality dimensions and metrics.

methods.name: Knowledge Cleaning
methods.description: A task in KG curation that aims to improve the correctness of KGs by detecting and correcting errors, distinguishing between verification and validation.

methods.name: Knowledge Enrichment
methods.description: A task in KG curation that aims to improve the completeness of KGs by adding new statements, involving duplicate detection and knowledge fusion.

methods.name: Verification of KGs
methods.description: The process of evaluating KGs with formal specifications of integrity constraints.

methods.name: Validation of KGs
methods.description: A critical task to provide accurate, correct, and reliable knowledge by evaluating whether an assertion is semantically correct and corresponds to the 'real' world.

methods.name: Duplicate Detection
methods.description: Identifying where two or more records in a single or various KGs are referring to the same entity.

methods.name: Knowledge Fusion
methods.description: Resolving conflicting property value assertions, also referred to as data fusion.

methods.name: Instance Matching
methods.description: A process run by the enrichment component to detect duplicates.

methods.name: Configuration Learning
methods.description: A module that tries to find a tuned configuration for instance matching.

methods.name: Entity Fusion
methods.description: A process supported by fusion strategies based on the assessment report of KGs, triggered by a duplicates report.

methods.name: Query-based approaches for Verification
methods.description: A category of methods for KG verification that apply query languages like SPARQL.

methods.name: Inference-based approaches for Verification
methods.description: A category of methods for KG verification that use inference rules.

methods.name: Structural languages for Verification
methods.description: A category of methods for KG verification that define property and class constraints.

methods.name: Internal approaches for Validation
methods.description: A category of methods for KG validation that rely on statements or triples existing within a KG.

methods.name: External approaches for Validation
methods.description: A category of methods for KG validation that use external sources like websites or Linked Open Data datasets.

methods.name: Outlier Detection Techniques
methods.description: Techniques used in internal validation to evaluate whether a property value is out of the assumed distribution.

methods.name: Embedding Models
methods.description: Models used in internal validation approaches.

methods.name: Topic Coherence
methods.description: A technique used in external validation approaches.

methods.name: Information Extraction
methods.description: A technique used in external validation approaches.

methods.name: Genetic Algorithm
methods.description: An algorithm that can automatically tune a configuration for duplicate detection.

methods.name: Schemarama
methods.description: A query-based approach for KG verification that applies the XPath method and uses SquisQL language.

methods.name: SPARQL Query Language
methods.description: A query language used in query-based approaches for KG verification.

methods.name: Simple Application-Specific Constraints
methods.description: A query-based approach for KG verification.

methods.name: SPARQL Inferencing Notation (SPIN)
methods.description: A query-based approach for KG verification.

methods.name: RDFUnit
methods.description: A query-based approach for KG verification.

methods.name: Shape Expressions (ShEx)
methods.description: A query-based approach for KG verification.

methods.name: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
methods.description: A query-based approach for KG verification.

methods.name: TreeHugger
methods.description: An inference-based approach for KG verification that uses XPath.

methods.name: Schematron rules
methods.description: An inference-based approach for KG verification that uses XPath.

methods.name: Stardog ICV
methods.description: An inference-based approach for KG verification that implements subsumption, domain-range, participation, cardinality, and property constraints.

methods.name: OSLC Resource Shape
methods.description: A structural language for KG verification that defines property constraints.

methods.name: Dublin Core Application Profiles
methods.description: A structural language for KG verification that defines constraints of values and cardinality of properties.

methods.name: RDF Data Description (RDD)
methods.description: A structural language for KG verification that defines property and class constraints.

methods.name: COPAAL
methods.description: A tool for internal validation that evaluates possible interesting relationships between entity pairs within a KG.

metrics.name: Accessibility
metrics.description: Evaluates if a KG is available, provides a public SPARQL endpoint, is retrievable in RDF, supports content negotiation, and describes a license.

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.description: Defines the syntactic and semantic validity of assertions contained in the KG.

metrics.name: Appropriate amount
metrics.description: Evaluates whether the KG contains knowledge for specific use case scenarios.

metrics.name: Believability
metrics.description: Measures whether the KG provides provenance information and is verifiable.

metrics.name: Completeness
metrics.description: Evaluates completeness in terms of schema and instance level for a specific use case.

metrics.name: Concise representation
metrics.description: Evaluates the use of blank nodes and reification.

metrics.name: Consistent representation
metrics.description: Detects the existence of disjoint inconsistencies of classes and schema restrictions in the KG.

metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness
metrics.description: Measures the degree to which accurate data is necessary.

metrics.name: Ease of manipulation
metrics.description: Evaluates the existence of documentation for manipulating the knowledge contained in the KG.

metrics.name: Ease of operation
metrics.description: Refers to the possibility of updating, downloading, and integrating the KG.

metrics.name: Ease of understanding
metrics.description: Evaluates whether self-descriptive URIs are used and knowledge is presented in more than one language.

metrics.name: Free-of-error
metrics.description: Refers to the total number of wrong and missing assertions contained in the KG.

metrics.name: Interoperability
metrics.description: Evaluates whether the KG re-uses standard vocabularies and complies with Linked Open Data 5 Star.

metrics.name: Objectivity
metrics.description: Defines the degree to which the KG is unbiased and impartial.

metrics.name: Relevancy
metrics.description: Evaluates the level of applicability, in terms of domain coverage, of the KG to a specific use case.

metrics.name: Reputation
metrics.description: Measures whether explicit trust ratings exist for the KG or qualifiers exist on KG’s statements.

metrics.name: Security
metrics.description: Evaluates the degree to which the KG uses a digital signature and verifies the identity of the publisher.

metrics.name: Timeliness
metrics.description: Measures the frequency of updates occurring in the KG and the validity period of its statements.

metrics.name: Traceability
metrics.description: Evaluates the degree to which the KG provides provenance information and keeps a log of edits and changes.

metrics.name: Variety
metrics.description: Refers to the degree to which the KG contains knowledge from different sources and various domains.

concepts.name: Knowledge Graph Curation
concepts.description: The process of improving the quality of knowledge graphs, also known as knowledge graph refinement.

concepts.name: Knowledge Graph Refinement
concepts.description: An alternative term for knowledge graph curation.

concepts.name: Knowledge Graph
concepts.description: Very large semantic nets that integrate various and heterogeneous information sources to represent knowledge about certain domains of discourse.

concepts.name: Quality of KGs
concepts.description: The overall status of a Knowledge Graph, which the curation framework aims to improve.

concepts.name: Knowledge Assessment (Concept)
concepts.description: A critical task in KG curation to provide reliable, correct, and complete knowledge.

concepts.name: Knowledge Cleaning (Concept)
concepts.description: A critical task in KG curation to provide reliable, correct, and complete knowledge, dealing with verification and validation.

concepts.name: Knowledge Enrichment (Concept)
concepts.description: A critical task in KG curation to provide reliable, correct, and complete knowledge, dealing with duplicate detection and knowledge fusion.

concepts.name: Quality Dimensions
concepts.description: A set of criteria for assessing the status of Knowledge Graphs.

concepts.name: Weights of Importance
concepts.description: User-defined degrees of importance for quality dimensions when curating KGs.

concepts.name: Correctness
concepts.description: An aspect of KG quality, improved by knowledge cleaning.

concepts.name: Completeness
concepts.description: An aspect of KG quality, improved by knowledge enrichment.

concepts.name: Verification
concepts.description: A knowledge cleaning task that evaluates schema conformance and integrity constraints of KGs.

concepts.name: Validation
concepts.description: A knowledge cleaning task that checks whether KGs accurately describe or represent the 'real' world.

concepts.name: Duplicates
concepts.description: Inconsistencies in KGs where two or more records refer to the same entity.

concepts.name: Conflicting Property Value Assertions
concepts.description: Situations where duplicated entities have a different value for the same property.

concepts.name: Data Fusion
concepts.description: The task of handling conflicting property value assertions.

concepts.name: Inconsistencies
concepts.description: General issues in KGs such as duplicates, wrong assertions, and missing values.

concepts.name: Wrong Assertions
concepts.description: Errors in KGs where statements are incorrect.

concepts.name: Missing Values
concepts.description: Errors in KGs where information is absent.

concepts.name: Syntactic Errors
concepts.description: Errors related to the syntax of data in KGs.

concepts.name: Semantic Errors
concepts.description: Errors related to the meaning or validity of data in KGs.

concepts.name: Schema Alignment
concepts.description: A semi-automatic mapping between a user's KG and another KG.

concepts.name: Dynamic Data
concepts.description: Fast-changing data, which adds complexity to KG curation.

concepts.name: Trade-off between completeness and correctness
concepts.description: A challenge in KG curation where improving one aspect may negatively impact the other.

concepts.name: Assessment Report
concepts.description: The outcome of the assessment process, stored for use in other components like entity fusion.

concepts.name: Integrity Constraints
concepts.description: Formal specifications used to verify KGs.

concepts.name: Expressivity of constraint languages
concepts.description: The capability of constraint languages, directly related to SPARQL expressivity.

concepts.name: Expressivity of SPARQL
concepts.description: The capability of the SPARQL query language.

concepts.name: Knowledge Assessment Frameworks
concepts.description: Frameworks that help to identify reliable and trustworthy KGs.

concepts.name: Duplicate Detection Frameworks
concepts.description: Frameworks that offer similarity metrics for duplicate detection.

concepts.name: reliable KGs
concepts.description: Knowledge Graphs identified as trustworthy and suitable for interlinking entities.

concepts.name: interlinking entities
concepts.description: The process of connecting entities between different Knowledge Graphs.

findings.name: Automation of quality dimensions is difficult
findings.description: Various quality dimensions can hardly be fully automated for technical or operational reasons.

findings.name: High cost of KG validation
findings.description: Validating KGs may lead to a high cost of deployment, due to its dependency on proprietary services.

findings.name: Performance reduction with open corpora
findings.description: If a validation framework uses open corpora (e.g. Wikipedia), its performance lows down.

findings.name: Complexity of dynamic data
findings.description: The complexity of dynamic data (i.e., fast-changing data) should be considered in KG curation.

findings.name: Prevention of errors during KG creation
findings.description: Fixing syntactic and semantic errors can be caught during the creation and hosting of KGs.

findings.name: Usability and maintenance issues of tools
findings.description: Many KG curation tools have usability issues, are complex to apply in different domains, and are often abandoned or no longer maintained.

findings.name: Knowledge assessment aids KG interlinking
findings.description: Knowledge assessment frameworks may help to identify reliable and trustworthy KGs, to which user’s KG can be interlinked.

findings.name: Simple similarity metrics in duplicate detection
findings.description: Most of the duplicate detection frameworks offer only simple similarity metrics, but complex cases need complex metrics.

findings.name: User-defined importance for quality dimensions
findings.description: Users can define the degree of importance of a quality dimension (i.e. weights) for assessing a KG.

findings.name: Lack of scalability in existing frameworks
findings.description: Existing frameworks are still lacking scalability to large KGs.

findings.name: Correction left to users
findings.description: Most approaches only detect errors or missing values but leave the correction part completely to users.

findings.name: Constraint language expressivity related to SPARQL
findings.description: The expressivity of constraint languages is directly related with the expressivity of SPARQL.
